poster_title: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
authors: Prateek Chhikara, Dev Khant, Saket Aryan, Taranjeet Singh, and Deshraj Yadav

panels.headline: Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in generating contextually coherent responses, but fixed context windows limit their ability to maintain coherence over prolonged multi-session dialogues.
content: LLMs generate contextually coherent responses.
Fixed context windows limit long-term coherence.
Memory mechanisms are essential for coherent, long-term human-AI interactions.
Proposed Mem0 and Mem0 g address these limitations.
Aims to improve practical deployment of LLM-driven AI agents.

panels.headline: LLMs lack persistent memory mechanisms, leading to inconsistent user interactions.
content: LLMs lack persistent memory mechanisms.
Extended context windows do not solve fundamental limitations.
Attention mechanisms degrade over distant tokens.
Effective retrieval of past information is challenging.
Proposed solutions must balance performance and efficiency.

panels.headline: Mem0 dynamically extracts, consolidates, and retrieves salient information from ongoing conversations.
content: Mem0: scalable memory-centric architecture.
Mem0 g: graph-based memory representations for advanced reasoning.

panels.headline: Evaluations on the LOCOMO benchmark.
content: LOCOMO benchmark used for evaluation.

Comparison against six baseline categories: memory-augmented systems, RAG with varying chunk sizes and k-values, full-context approaches, open-source solutions, proprietary models, and dedicated memory management platforms.
panels.figure_caption: Performance comparison of memory-enabled systems across different question types in the LOCOMO dataset.

panels.headline: Mem0 achieves 26% relative improvements in the LLM-as-a-Judge metric over OpenAI.
content: Mem0 outperforms all existing memory systems.
26% relative improvements in LLM-as-a-Judge metric over OpenAI.
Mem0 g achieves 2% higher overall score than base Mem0.
91% lower p95 latency and 90% token cost savings compared to full-context approaches.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison of total response latency at p50 and p95 across different memory methods.

panels.headline: Structured, persistent memory mechanisms are critical for long-term conversational coherence.
content: Structured, persistent memory mechanisms are critical for long-term coherence.
Mem0 and Mem0 g balance advanced reasoning and practical deployment.
These approaches pave the way for more reliable and efficient LLM-driven AI agents.
Future work: improve conversation summary and recent message context quality.
Potential for broader applications in AI-driven systems.
